clue.text: In two senses, bear with English poet

parts.note: Rupert is the famous cartoon bear of children's annuals
to bear something is to tolerate it, to brook it

explanation.surface: A bear keeps company with an English writer of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In two senses' tells you the single word 'bear' is used twice: once as the cartoon bear's name, once as the verb meaning tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: The man named was a First World War poet, author of 'The Soldier'.

clue.text: Reddish deer seen around country house

indicators.note: the deer word goes around the house word, enclosing it

parts.note: a roe is a small deer
a seat is a large country house, the home of a landed family

explanation.surface: A deer is spotted near a stately home.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rose-coloured is a pinkish red, a synonym of reddish.

clue.text: Sacred picture that is accepted by school organisation

indicators.note: being accepted by something means being taken inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: PTA is the parent-teacher association of a school
ie is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A religious painting is taken in by a parents' group at school.
explanation.definitionFit: A pieta is a painting or sculpture of the Virgin Mary holding the dead Christ, a sacred image.

clue.text: Wicked judge accepting point in favour of bandit leader

indicators.note: taking in other letters, so the judging word surrounds the rest

parts.note: to rate something is to judge or assess it
E, east, is a point of the compass
pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A corrupt judge takes a point in favour of a gang's ringleader.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprobate is an unprincipled scoundrel, so as an adjective it means wicked or depraved.

clue.text: Happened to live on hill

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: to be is to exist, to live
a fell is a hill or upland moor, especially in northern England

explanation.surface: Someone takes up residence on a hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that befell a person was what happened to them, an old-fashioned synonym.

clue.text: Musical fine if shortened

explanation.surface: A show tune would be fine if it were cut down.
explanation.walkthrough: The state's postal abbreviation is OK, which also means fine; so the title, shortened, says fine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rodgers and Hammerstein show of 1943 is a famous musical; its state is abbreviated to two letters meaning all right.

clue.text: After rising, frolic around a village

indicators.note: the turned frolic word goes around the letter a
in a down clue, rising means the word reads from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a lark is a bit of fun, a frolic

explanation.surface: Having got up, someone frolics around a village.
explanation.definitionFit: A kraal is a traditional enclosed settlement in southern Africa, a village.

clue.text: Accurate, as writers to the Editor often claim to be?

definitions.text: as writers to the Editor often claim to be?

explanation.surface: Letter writers sign off claiming loyalty to the editor.
explanation.walkthrough: Letters to an editor traditionally end 'Yours faithfully'.
explanation.definitionFit: A faithful copy is an accurate one; and correspondents sign off as loyal, true to the editor.

clue.text: Tinker bringing in peg that's very hard

indicators.note: the tinker word takes the peg word inside itself

parts.note: Christopher Sly is the drunken tinker in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew
a tee is the small peg a golf ball sits on

explanation.surface: A tinker brings in a peg made of something extremely tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tinker' looks like a verb meaning fiddle with, but it names Shakespeare's tinker Sly.
explanation.definitionFit: Steely means hard as steel, unyielding.

clue.text: Needing lots of bread to soak

explanation.surface: Something costly is ready for a good soaking.
explanation.walkthrough: Bread is slang for money, so steep prices need lots of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep price is a high one, demanding much money; and to steep something is to immerse it, leaving it to soak.

clue.text: After season abroad, some go to pieces

indicators.note: the piece meaning some comes after the season word

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn, so it is the season abroad
a part of something is some of it

explanation.surface: After an autumn spent overseas, some people have a breakdown.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall apart is an idiom for losing composure, collapsing emotionally.

clue.text: Religious leader having a stroke has foreign nurse around

indicators.note: the nurse word sits around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: an ayah is a nursemaid in India
a toll is a stroke of a bell

explanation.surface: A cleric has a stroke and a nurse from abroad stays by him.
explanation.definitionFit: An ayatollah is a senior Shia cleric in Iran, a religious leader.

clue.text: Drunk about a couple of pints? Less

parts.note: lit is slang for drunk
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A drunk comments on a couple of pints, then asks for less.
explanation.definitionFit: A metric measure of about 1.76 pints, so a little under two pints.

clue.text: Slip back to catch one glimpse

indicators.note: the turned word catches a letter, holding it inside
back means the slip word is read in reverse

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or minor error
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone slips backwards trying to catch a glimpse.
explanation.definitionFit: Espial is an old word for spying or catching sight of something, a glimpse.

clue.text: Under pressure, striking forward and taking a dive

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics
lunging is thrusting forward to strike

explanation.surface: A fencer under pressure lunges, then takes a dive.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the rest sits under the pressure letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Plunging means diving headlong, taking a dive.

clue.text: Not too much greasy food for the children

parts.note: small means not large in amount
a fry is a fried meal, such as a full fry-up

explanation.surface: A small portion of fried food is enough for the kids.
explanation.definitionFit: Small fry is an idiom for young children, or for unimportant people.

clue.text: Be' prompt in personal appearance with instrument

parts.note: looks are a person's appearance
a harp is a stringed musical instrument

explanation.surface: Be punctual, look smart, and bring your instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Look sharp is an idiom for hurry up, be quick.

clue.text: A cloth edge around sleeve flapping unnecessarily

indicators.note: the cloth edge word goes around the sleeve word

parts.note: a list is the selvage, the edge of a piece of cloth
a sleeve is the arm of a garment

explanation.surface: A piece of cloth edging around a sleeve flaps in the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flapping' here is in a flap, panicking.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarmist spreads needless fear, someone panicking without cause.

clue.text: Trim back everything that may be material in court

parts.note: to prune is to trim back plants

indicators.note: back means the everything word is read in reverse

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A gardener cuts back everything that might be relevant in a legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' looks like legal evidence, but it is fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Prunella is a strong fabric once used for barristers' gowns, so cloth worn in court.

clue.text: With misrepresentation, stir up pedant

indicators.note: a misrepresentation gives a distorted version, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stickler stirs up trouble by misrepresenting things.
explanation.definitionFit: A purist insists on strict correctness, a pedant.

clue.text: Coiffeur may use it for wave

explanation.surface: A hairdresser reaches for something to create a wave.
explanation.definitionFit: A roller is a curler used by hairdressers; it is also a long heavy sea wave.

clue.text: After fight between boxers, a set-end needed

definitions.text: After fight between boxers, a set-end needed

parts.words: After fight between boxers, a set-end needed
parts.note: an inconclusive bout calls for the two fighters to meet again

explanation.surface: After an indecisive bout, the fighters must meet again.
explanation.definitionFit: A second contest between the same opponents settles an unresolved fight.

clue.text: Give advance warning appreciation of services won't be forthcoming

definitions.text: appreciation of services won't be forthcoming

explanation.surface: A warning that no gratuity will be paid.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase, 'tip' (gratuity) is 'off', cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a secret warning is an idiom with the same words; and with gratuity cancelled, no thanks for service arrives.

clue.text: Star set on small Eastern state

indicators.note: in an across clue the set word is placed on, after, the state

parts.note: RI is Rhode Island, the smallest US state, on the east coast
to gel is to set firm

explanation.surface: A star sets over a small state in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigel is the bright blue star in the constellation Orion.

clue.text: One's fleeced as everything gina shopping centre goes up

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: Shoppers feel fleeced as all the prices at the mall rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Everything in' is surface: the mall contains 'all', and 'One's fleeced' is a woolly animal, not a cheated shopper.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American animal sheared for its wool, so a creature that is shorn.

clue.text: Minor star, exploding, falls from the sky

indicators.note: an explosion scatters the pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A minor star explodes and debris falls to earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy downpour, a storm of rain coming down from above.

clue.text: To be sedentary partly makes one this

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Sitting about all day will make you fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Being very overweight is what a sedentary life can lead to.

clue.text: Romans in a different part, of their peninsula

indicators.note: different means changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Romans in another region of the Italian peninsula.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiny republic lies within Italy, so it is a part of the Romans' peninsula.

clue.text: Ward off right covered by a special sort of doctor

indicators.note: being covered by a word puts the right letter inside it

parts.note: a vet is a doctor for animals

explanation.surface: Keep the right protected by a special kind of doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert a danger is to fend it off, prevent it.

clue.text: Interjection, for example, of soundbite

explanation.surface: A soundbite contains an exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, a soundbite is a piece of what is said.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar names word classes such as noun, verb and interjection; a soundbite is a fragment of a talk.
